title: The Rule of 72: Time Is the Hidden Multiplier

beats.say: A $200 monthly habit, kept for 30 years at 7%, becomes $243,994.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a small stack of burnt-orange paper coins at the bottom left rising step by step into a towering teal paper coin column on the right, stretched along a torn paper timeline strip

beats.say: But you only paid in $72,000, so where did the rest come from?
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: the tall coin tower split by a torn line, a short burnt-orange base section and a much larger teal upper section, with a black ink paper question mark shape hovering beside the teal part

beats.say: Not your salary, not a raise, not a side hustle, it came from time.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a paper paycheck envelope and a paper briefcase pushed aside to the edges while a large teal paper clock sits in the center, its hands pouring paper coins downward

beats.say: And there's a shortcut that roughly shows how time multiplies money, called the Rule of 72.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a burnt-orange paper key cut in the shape of a clock hand, sliding into a teal paper lock on a vault door made of layered paper

beats.say: Divide 72 by your yearly growth rate, and you get the years to double.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a black ink paper division bar slicing a long torn calendar strip into equal sections, each section ending with a single paper coin turning into two

beats.say: At 4%, money doubles in 18 years, slow, like a long winter.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a tiny paper snail carrying a burnt-orange paper coin across a very long stack of torn calendar pages, teal paper snowflakes drifting down

beats.say: At 8%, it's 9 years, at 12%, just 6 years.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: three paper calendar stacks side by side shrinking from tall to short, each topped by a coin splitting into two, the shortest stack accented in teal

beats.say: Now stack those doublings, each one bigger than the last, because doubling compounds on itself.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a paper staircase where each step is twice as tall as the one before, burnt-orange coins on the low steps and teal coins piling high on the top steps

beats.say: That's why a $10,000 lump sum at 7% for 30 years reaches $76,123.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a single burnt-orange paper seed planted in torn paper soil growing into a tall teal paper tree whose leaves are paper coins

beats.say: Here's the catch, the rule works in reverse, against you, through inflation.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: the paper clock from earlier spinning backwards, its teal hands now snipping small pieces off a burnt-orange paper banknote like scissors

beats.say: At 3% inflation, $100 is worth just $55 in today's money after 20 years.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a full burnt-orange paper banknote on the left and a torn, shrunken version on the right, with a trail of torn paper scraps falling between them along a calendar strip

beats.say: So time is either multiplying your money, or quietly shrinking it, never neutral.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a paper clock splitting down the middle, the teal half sprouting growing coin stacks, the burnt-orange half crumbling into torn paper dust

beats.say: Feeling behind is mostly about time, and time is the variable you still control.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a paper cutout hand silhouette, no face, turning a large teal paper dial shaped like a clock, burnt-orange coins lining up in order as it turns

beats.say: Today, divide 72 by any rate you see, and picture the years it really means.
beats.visual: torn-paper collage, hand-cut paper cutouts with drop shadows, visible paper fibre and torn white edges, warm off-white background, black ink, one burnt-orange accent and one teal accent, flat editorial illustration, no photorealism, no text, no letters, no faces: a torn paper magnifying glass held over a percentage-shaped paper cutout, revealing inside the lens a long teal calendar strip unrolling into the distance

caption: You only paid in $72,000, but it grew to $243,994. The difference wasn't salary. It was time. ⏳
description: The Rule of 72 is a simple mental shortcut: divide 72 by a yearly growth rate to estimate how many years money takes to double. This explainer shows why time, not income, is the hidden multiplier, and how the same math works against you through inflation. Educational content only, not financial advice.
first_comment: Try it now: pick any rate you've seen this week, a savings account, a loan, inflation, and divide 72 by it. What number did you get? 👇
